name: integrated_access_v4
status_detail: DEMO-ONLY (multi-party phase 2: 3 contributors + public beacon; phase 1 is a public ceremony): no production audit of the ceremony or the circuit; not for production

ptau.provenance: PSE Perpetual Powers of Tau contribution 0080, prepared for phase 2 with a beacon (Ethereum beacon chain slot 7,325,000 randao_reveal, 31 iterations); downloaded over HTTPS from PSE's official bucket (https://pse-trusted-setup-ppot.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/pot28_0080); header power 15, ceremonyPower 28, sections 12-15 present, 62 contributions in section 7; section 7 contains the published challenge_0080 hash (d9ec6fad4a7a7e3358a0c4bed7171622...) at offset 90185 and challenge_0081 hash (4bf672f3ba1de1bb6105e1ab88359612...) at offset 91706, matching 0080_carter_response/README.md; blake2b-512 pinned on first download 2026-11-08 (PSE publishes no hash for prepared files); full snarkjs powersoftau verify not run (2^28-point initial hash infeasible in the sandbox)

contributors.participant: P1 circuits - simulated by agent on same machine
P2 identity - simulated by agent on same machine
P3 gateway - simulated by agent on same machine

phase2.entropy: per contributor: /dev/urandom (64 bytes) on stdin, mixed by snarkjs with crypto.randomBytes
phase2.limitation: multi-party phase 2 (3 contributors: P1 circuits - simulated by agent on same machine, P2 identity - simulated by agent on same machine, P3 gateway - simulated by agent on same machine): sound as long as at least one contributor generated their entropy honestly and destroyed it; all of them colluding (or all being compromised) could forge proofs
